body: Tuesday, July 28 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed is in a hawkish hold posture with the FOMC meeting beginning today and a decision due tomorrow. The 10Y yield is surging at 4.59% (+22 bps vs 4W ago), the 2Y at 4.31% (prior close, +24 bps vs 4W), producing a +34bps curve that is positively sloped but still flat by historical standards — a near-parallel bear move (spread only 3 bps wider) that signals hawkish re-pricing across the curve, not easing expectations. An Iran war is actively adding supply-shock risk to an already sticky inflation backdrop. Fiscal stance remains expansionary with no consolidation in sight.

New / Most Important: The FOMC meeting began today with the consensus expecting a hold, but the signal feed reveals an active debate about whether a rate hike is on the table — CBS, Yahoo Finance, and USA Today all flagged the possibility. Kevin Warsh's press conference is being treated as a signal event in its own right. This is structurally new: for the first time in this cycle, the Fed's decision is genuinely two-way (hold vs. hike) rather than the prior framing (hold vs. cut). The Iran conflict is the catalyst forcing this reappraisal — energy-driven inflation transmission into core goods and services threatens to un-anchor expectations. The US goods trade deficit shrank but is still expected to weigh on Q2 GDP, creating a stagflationary pocket where growth disappoints even as inflation re-accelerates. Oil at 78.66 (↑11.2% vs 4W) is the transmission mechanism. VIX at 17.95 in COMPLACENCY regime is dangerously mispriced against this two-way policy risk.

Playbook ✓: S&P 500 at 7440 (↑1.2%) holding up on earnings — broad index resilience despite chip stock rout is textbook late-cycle rotation.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The real divergence is that the market is pricing complacency (VIX ↓2.5%) while a genuine rate hike is being discussed by credible outlets. Household wealth has never leaned this hard on the stock market per Investopedia — just as AI bubble fears hit equities. Rate-sensitive data contradict the VIX signal — the 30-year mortgage rate at 6.58% is the highest in nearly a year and gold holds near all-time highs — suggesting real-economy hedging is happening outside equities while equity vol is suppressed. This is the kind of cross-asset divergence that precedes violent repricing.

Macro Stance: The ECB held rates at 2.25% on July 23, keeping the door explicitly open for further hikes. The policy stance has decisively pivoted from the easing cycle that markets expected earlier in 2026 — this is now a re-tightening regime driven by Iran-war energy price transmission into European inflation. Fiscal policy is fragmented across member states with Germany's economy only growing modestly in Q2.

New / Most Important: This is structurally the biggest shift in European macro this year. The ECB held last week but traders now see a September rate hike as the base case per CNBC and FT reporting. The ECB explicitly cited the Iran war's energy price spike as the inflation driver that arrested their easing path. This marks a full reversal of the 2025 cutting cycle — the ECB is now re-hiking into a weak German economy. For capital flows, this creates a nasty trap: European equities face margin compression from both rising rates AND an energy cost shock, while the euro may strengthen on rate differentials, further hurting exporters. The Nikkei tumbled 4.31% while DAX gained — a rare divergence suggesting European equity markets are front-running the hawkish pivot as EUR-strength benefiting domestic purchasing power. European credit spreads should widen as the ECB re-tightens into stagnant growth — watch subordinated bank paper.

Playbook ✓: Energy price spike flowing through to ECB hawkishness is textbook supply-shock transmission.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The DAX gaining while the ECB signals hikes breaks the normal playbook — likely driven by rotation out of Asia/tech into European value and defense names. This divergence won't hold if September hike materializes.

Macro Stance: The PBOC is easing through volume, not price: rather than cut benchmark rates, the central bank added the most liquidity in five months (Bloomberg, [Jul 23]) and is running overnight reverse repos alongside a 500b-yuan MLF operation, injecting a total of 2.1 trillion yuan (Reuters, [Jul 24]; China Daily, [Jul 24]). The currency is being managed tightly: the PBOC marginally lowered the daily yuan fix versus the dollar (TradingPedia, [Jul 27]) while Europe scrutinises the yuan's value (Bloomberg, [Jul 21]). Prices are split: June CPI rose only 1% (Global Times, [Jul 9]) while PPI climbed 4.1% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 8]), a near four-year high that squeezes manufacturers (Reuters, [Jul 8]).

PMIs & Activity: The last official read is June: manufacturing PMI 50.3 and non-manufacturing 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]); July's numbers are the next test (ING Think, [Jul 23]). Q2 GDP grew 4.3%, below the official target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]); June industrial output rose 5.3% y/y and retail sales returned to growth (BusinessLine, [Jul 15]), but first-half retail sales were up just 1.3% (Ecns.cn, [Jul 15]) and investment slid as infrastructure joined property (Caixin Global, [Jul 15]), while June exports surged 27% from a year earlier (AP News, [Jul 14]). The June profit data sharpen the split: first-half industrial profits rose 18.7% as a tech boom masks the property slump (Caixin Global, [Jul 27]), chipmaking profits soared 2,500% (South China Morning Post, [Jul 27]), yet growth is the slowest this year (Financial Times, [Jul 26]) and payment arrears and "involution" still slam traditional industries (South China Morning Post, [Jul 27]). July car sales are set to fall 16.8% (GlobalChinaEV, [Jul 27]).

Credit Impulse: June new bank loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]) and credit growth missed as the PBOC flagged a "new normal" (Caixin Global, [Jul 16]); household loans fell by 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]). The finance minister's claim that fiscal-financial synergy leveraged over 17 trillion yuan in new loans (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 22]) is not a contradiction: the volume is policy-directed corporate and state-linked lending while households pay down. Pricing is loosening quietly: banks are breaking with the lending benchmark (Bloomberg, [Jul 24]) and the biggest lenders launched the first repo-linked loans (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]). Read: headline impulse flat, household impulse negative, price easing by the back door.

Property: June new home prices fell at a slower pace (Reuters, [Jul 14]) and first-tier prices extended a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Jul 15]), but resale prices fell faster (Reuters, [Jun 30]) and property investment slumped 18 percent y/y in January–June (The Standard (HK), [Jul 15]). Foreign capital is exiting, with KKR and AEW looking to join the sell-off wave (The Real Deal, [Jul 22]), and regulators curbed a loan structure used by distressed developers (Bloomberg, [Jul 22]) and offshore loans for local real estate firms (The Standard (HK), [Jul 23]). Vanke completed extensions on its 2026 public bonds (Caixin Global, [Jul 23]) with a RMB 519 million loan from Shenzhen Metro at 2.29% (BigGo Finance, [Jul 21]): state shareholders, not buyers, hold it together.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing pledged stronger policy support (TradingView, [Jul 21]) yet clings to austerity despite the slowdown (Bloomberg, [Jul 22]), and growth is set to slow in the second half as it avoids broad stimulus (Yahoo Finance Australia, [Jul 25]); the July Politburo meeting, still ahead, is the marker for the growth commitment (Bloomberg, [Jul 23]). On trade, China says the US pledged to cap replacement tariffs at 20% (Bloomberg, [Jul 27]); it condemned the new Section 301 tariffs but held off on retaliation (South China Morning Post, [Jul 27]), opposed the "forced labour" tariffs (Reuters, [Jul 27]) and is drawing lines on tariffs and AI ahead of the Xi-Trump summit (Bloomberg, [Jul 27]). Europe is the harder front: 14 EU entities went onto its export control list (Reuters, [Jul 24]) and Italy's machine tool sector wants tougher EU trade rules (Reuters, [Jul 27]).

Markets & Flows: China's tech self-reliance is now moving global prices. CXMT vaulted to the top of China's valuations with a 466% Shanghai debut (Reuters, [Jul 27]), ASML slid on a report of China starting DUV tool production (Bloomberg, [Jul 27]) and Asia stocks tumbled as China chip advances rattled sentiment (Investing.com, [Jul 27]). Chinese tech firms have raised $27.13 bln in Hong Kong (Reuters, [Jul 27]), but the Hang Seng opened shy of the 25,000 mark (The Standard (HK), [Jul 27]), and a Big Short trader's bearish AI bets are testing China's stock support (South China Morning Post, [Jul 27]).

New / Most Important: A 20% cap on replacement tariffs, if Washington confirms it, would remove the tail risk on China's export engine, and Beijing's choice not to retaliate shows it wants that deal before the summit. That matters because exports and AI-linked profits are all that is carrying growth; the domestic side still needs the Politburo to move.

Playbook ✓: LPR on hold, liquidity easing, export-led profits, weak property and a calm tariff response are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Markets read China as an AI supply-chain winner while its old economy weakens. The transmission is uneven: China's chip advances hit Korea's memory names, part of why the Kospi is down 10.8%, while an 18 percent property-investment slump keeps construction-linked bulk demand fading, a drag on AUD and iron ore. Breakingviews argues China can keep dousing world oil prices ([Jul 27]), yet the oil spike remains a terms-of-trade negative for a major importer. European exporters face the surplus, and EM inflows ride IPO euphoria rather than a PMI or credit upturn.

Macro Stance: The BOJ held rates at 1% and upgraded its GDP forecast, but is signaling more rate hikes ahead as price pressures build. The yen is near 40-year lows against the dollar, creating a self-reinforcing inflation loop through import prices. The BOJ meeting on Friday is the next catalyst.

New / Most Important: This is a structurally important moment. The Nikkei tumbled 4.31% in a single session while the BOJ simultaneously signals more hikes — a classic policy tightening into equity weakness dynamic. The yen stuck near 160 despite hawkish BOJ signaling reveals that the US-Japan rate differential is still too wide for the yen to respond to domestic tightening alone. Early rate-rise bets are increasing per Nikkei Asia, and Japanese life insurers are rotating into yen-denominated products — this is a massive capital flow signal. When Japan's ~$4 trillion life insurance sector repatriates from foreign bonds into JGBs, it creates a structural bid for the yen and selling pressure on US Treasuries. This is one of the most important cross-border flow dynamics in global macro right now: BOJ hikes → life insurer repatriation → UST selling → higher US yields → stronger dollar → weaker yen → more BOJ pressure. A reflexive loop.

Playbook ✓: Weak yen + hawkish signaling is textbook for the BOJ normalization path.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Nikkei down 4.31% suggests the equity market is no longer treating BOJ hikes as a positive normalization signal — it's becoming genuinely contractionary for risk assets. Friday's decision is binary risk.

Macro Stance: The RBA is keeping a rate hike explicitly on the table while acknowledging the economy is cooling. Bond markets are betting on rates staying higher for longer, with rate cuts pushed out further. Housing has eased more than the RBA anticipated.

New / Most Important: The RBA governor issued an "unusually candid warning to every household" — this is notable communication escalation. The RBA's chief expressed genuine uncertainty about whether rates are high enough to tame inflation, per Reuters. This is structurally hawkish ambiguity: markets expected a dovish pivot from housing weakness, but the RBA is instead signaling it may need to hike further. The Australian Dollar analysis confirms "RBA keeps hike option alive." For an economy this rate-sensitive (massive household mortgage debt), this is a painful equilibrium — the RBA can't ease even as housing cracks.

Playbook ✓: Higher-for-longer narrative extending is consistent with commodity-linked inflation persistence.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Housing easing "more than anticipated" while the RBA still can't pivot dovish — this is the stagflationary bind where the central bank is trapped between asset deflation and goods inflation.

Macro Stance: The cut debate is moving from "when" to "whether". Citi now expects CPI to reach 3% as early as July on fuel prices (PAP Biznes, [Jul 28]) and Business Insider Polska warned inflation could breach the NBP's limit with more price rises to come [Jul 28], while FXMAG modelled diesel at 9 or 10 zł and inflation near 10% in a long Middle East conflict [Jul 24]. That lands on a Council already turning: Kotecki said the inflation picture is diverging from the NBP projection and it is too early to promise a September cut (pb.pl, [Jul 23]), a hawk called the earlier cuts premature (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 21]) and one member put hikes ahead of cuts (Super Biznes, [Jul 21]); wnp.pl summed it up as a big change on rates from what was supposed to happen [Jul 23]. The backward-looking data remain strong: inflation fell to 3% (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Jul 22]), yet June retail sales grew 6.2% y/y against a 5.2% consensus (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 22]), ING BSK sees Q2 GDP near 3.8% y/y (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 22]), Business Insider Polska noted no large EU economy is growing faster [Jul 28]. Unemployment fell in June (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 23]) while wage growth slowed to its lowest since 2021 (FOCUS ON Business, [Jul 23]).

Markets: Rotation, not breakout. After Monday's Żabka collapse of around 14% on Seven & i ending stake talks (Briefs Finance, [Jul 27]), Tuesday saw the WIG and WIG20 close slightly lower with Dino sharply higher (XYZ, [Jul 28]): Orlen fell 3% while Dino gained 4.13% and CD Projekt 3.67% (FXMAG, [Jul 28]), Orlen and PGE weighed most (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 28]) and PGE slipped back below 10 zł (DNA Rynków, [Jul 28]). Orlen paid a record dividend of 8 zł per share (Bankier.pl, [Jul 28]). The card still shows an energy-led month: Orlen at 151.0 is up 3.0% on the week and 20.8% over four weeks, PGE at 10.25 is up 8.1% and 8.2%, Allegro at 45.0 is up 21.1% in four weeks and LPP at 20600 is up 3.5% and 11.4%; banks are firmer, PKO at 108.0 (+1.2% 1W, +4.5% 4W) and Pekao at 237.6 (+2.2% 1W), and KGHM at 302.5 is still 5.8% below four weeks ago. EPOL closed at 41.07, up 1.5% on the week and 7.3% over four weeks. The zloty gave back ground: USD/PLN closed at 3.7994 (+0.1% 1W, +1.2% 4W) and EUR/PLN at 4.3195 (-0.3% 1W, +0.8% 4W), and CEO Magazyn reported the dollar breaking 3.80 PLN as markets wait for the Fed [Jul 28]; Bankier.pl sees no let-up from a strong dollar and dear euro [Jul 28]. Bonds remain the sore point after yields jumped sharply late last week (Bankier.pl, [Jul 24]); the Treasury published its August savings-bond offer (Gov.pl, [Jul 27]), which Subiektywnie o finansach reads as a test of whether banks will pay savers better ([Jul 27]).

Fiscal & Politics: The finance ministry retreated on both flanks in one day. It dropped a package of PIT and CIT anti-avoidance measures covering lump-sum taxation, company cars, the housing relief and IP Box (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 28]; Prawo.pl, [Jul 28]) and at the same time published costings for a higher tax-free allowance, running to billions of zloty (Interia Biznes, [Jul 28]; TVN24, [Jul 28]), with Business Insider Polska putting the gain at up to 433 zł per taxpayer [Jul 28]. This comes after debt reached 61.6% of GDP, the third fastest rise in the EU (XYZ, [Jul 21]), Treasury debt passed 2.1 trillion zł (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 24]) and Rzeczpospolita wrote that Poland forgot to deleverage and will now find it hard to cut debt and deficit [Jul 28]; Arak sees more than 70% of GDP by end-2027 (Filary Biznesu, [Jul 26]). The fuel standoff continues: the windfall-profits tax sits at the Constitutional Tribunal with 4 billion zł of CPN funding blocked (Gov.pl, [Jul 27]), the Prime Minister spoke of bringing the CPN package back and Orlen responded (Money.pl, [Jul 28]), the government is considering regulated fuel prices (GlobEnergia, [Jul 28]).

Corporate & Sectors: Bank Millennium posted more than 400 million zł of profit but management is cautious on the autumn (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 28]), set aside 61 million zł more for consumer-credit disputes (Bankier.pl, [Jul 28]) and expects a slight NIM decline with cost of risk possibly below 40-50 bp (Bankier.pl, [Jul 28]). The CJEU hardened its WIBOR case law (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 28]), millions of loan contracts must be amended within two months (Money.pl, [Jul 28]) and banks surprised clients by raising deposit rates (Interia Biznes, [Jul 28]). Allegro is buying back 100 million zł of its shares (wirtualnemedia.pl, [Jul 28]) a day after naming Katarzyna Ostap-Tomann CFO (Parkiet, [Jul 27]). LPP Logistics opened a Romanian distribution centre sized for 35 million items (Strefa Biznesu, [Jul 28]). PGE confirmed the Rybnik coal units run to 2028 (Dziennik Zachodni, [Jul 27]).

Geopolitics & Security: Poland denied any territorial claims on Ukraine and reaffirmed support for Kyiv (logos-pres.md, [Jul 28]) and the army took delivery of new weapons as Ukrainians flagged a major threat (Forsal.pl, [Jul 28]). The backdrop is Belarusian special forces on the Ukrainian border (TVP Info, [Jul 22]) and troops reported at the Polish frontier (Kresy24.pl, [Jul 23]), Warsaw's warning that Russia may use captured Ukrainian drones against Poland and the Baltics (Defense News, [Jul 21]).

New / Most Important: The finance ministry's double retreat is the development: shelving PIT and CIT tightening while costing a higher tax-free allowance means the fiscal response to debt above 60% of GDP is looser, not tighter, on the same day Citi pulled its 3% CPI call forward to July. The NBP is being left as the only brake, which is why Kotecki's projection warning matters more than the June retail beat.  |  Playbook ✓: Hold stands; the ECB's hawkish hold narrows the NBP's room to diverge. Prefer banks and domestic retail, which absorbed Tuesday's rotation out of Orlen and PGE, and keep duration short.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The dollar above 3.80 and yields at highs say risk-off, yet EPOL is up 7.3% in four weeks and Dino and CD Projekt rallied into a flat index; Orlen's record 8 zł dividend against a 3% drop and a revived CPN package says the market is pricing the politics, not the payout.

Macro Stance: Pakistan's SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% citing inflation and geopolitical risks limiting room for easing — a direct Iran war casualty. South Korea's Kospi crashed 10.8%, the standout EM risk event this week.

New / Most Important: The Kospi collapse is extraordinary in magnitude and signals severe semiconductor/AI exposure unwind in Asia. This is likely connected to the global chip stock rout, but a 10.8% weekly decline suggests forced selling or margin calls beyond fundamentals. Pakistan's hold confirms the Iran war is directly constraining EM monetary easing cycles — oil importers with current account deficits are the most exposed. Capital flow implications: rising US yields + surging oil = classic EM squeeze conditions. The Dollar Funding Stress headline from Equiti confirms FX liquidity risk is building.

Playbook ✓: EM under pressure from rising DM rates is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Kospi -10.8% is far beyond normal rotation — this looks like a structural break in the Korea semiconductor premium trade.

Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 at 27,844 (↓4.4% vs 4W) is the worst-performing major US index, driven by the chip rout while the rest of the market barely flinches — a concentrated tech selloff that tests how far stocks and the economy rely on the AI boom.

Reported: IBM cut its annual revenue growth forecast as customers prioritize AI infrastructure spending (Reuters, [Jul 22]). ServiceNow raised its annual subscription revenue forecast again on AI-driven demand (Reuters, [Jul 22]). F5 lifted its outlook as AI demand fuelled a 32% surge in systems revenue (BigGo Finance, [Jul 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: Apple — Goldman raised its target ahead of Q3, expecting outperformance on iPhone and Mac revenue (TipRanks, [Jul 27]). Oracle — landed a $7 billion Pentagon software contract (TIKR.com, [Jul 24]), contracted revenue still to reach earnings.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Mega-cap tech is underperforming while the S&P holds up and the Russell/Nasdaq ratio climbs 2.6% — breadth expansion that is bullish for the broad market but bearish for the concentrated AI trade. Winners are rotating, not vanishing: software rebounded on the AI rotation, with Workday up 10% (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 27]).

Narrative: Meta backing open models alongside Nvidia is a strategic pivot that could commoditize AI inference and shift value from model providers to platforms with distribution moats; Meta reports this week.

Reported: Alphabet beat Q2 revenue estimates but dropped 5% on a $205B capex outlook (MLQ.ai, [Jul 23]). Vodafone raised guidance on its Safaricom deal (WSJ, [Jul 27]). Charter beat estimates, but its subscriber losses suggest a bleak future for cable (Barron's, [Jul 24]).
EPS Upside Watch: Meta — Deutsche Bank expects strong earnings as AI tools boost advertiser returns (TIKR.com, [Jul 26]), the ad-pricing lever behind an EPS surprise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Big Tech earnings are slamming into a market in revolt over AI spending (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 26]): Alphabet's beat-and-drop shows revenue no longer protects a platform stock, so capex discipline is what Meta must show.

Narrative: A 10Y at 4.59% (+22 bps vs 4W) lifts asset yields, but a +34bps curve, little changed over four weeks, is too flat for a strong NIM backdrop; capital-markets revenue is the engine, with Morgan Stanley's trading boom in focus.

Reported: Capital One topped earnings estimates as credit losses fell and the Discover integration progressed (Quartz, [Jul 21]). BNP Paribas lifted its dividend as revenue and profit beat (WSJ, [Jul 23]). American Express beat and raised its revenue forecast (Quartz, [Jul 24]), and most US banks beat forecasts on favourable revenue trends (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: Visa — its Q3 report is flagged as a potential catalyst (TradingView, [Jul 23]). Morgan Stanley — named the new trading leader, with wealth management, trading and higher rates a triple tailwind.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The H2 2026 distressed-debt outlook, citing an elevated cost of capital and software debt, is the warning: banks earning more from higher rates while distressed credit builds is the classic late-cycle setup — earnings up today, provisions up tomorrow — and a complacent VIX makes credit hedges cheap.

Narrative: WTI at 78.66 (↑11.2% vs 4W) is the standout mover on the Iran war, and drillers added rigs for a fourth week. With China's Q2 GDP at 4.3% and its industrial profit growth the slowest this year, this is a supply shock, not demand-led.

Reported: TotalEnergies posted its strongest profit in nearly three years on the Iran war (Reuters, [Jul 23]). SLB raised its outlook as data-centre revenue leapt 80% and analysts lifted targets (BigGo Finance, [Jul 27]). Baker Hughes beat Q2 forecasts and its shares climbed (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: US majors — Big Oil is set to reap a profit bonanza from soaring fuel prices (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 22]). Chevron — the integrated major best placed to capture the supply-shock premium while keeping downstream margin discipline, and it is eyeing a buy point.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Intraday oil relief rallies are being faded while the four-week trend stays up. Rig adds should eventually cap prices, but Baker Hughes flags lower spending by oil and gas producers in 2026 (Reuters, [Jul 27]) — capital discipline keeps the supply response slow, and the war premium matters more.
Narrative: The Russell 2000 at 2953 (↓1.9% vs 4W) suggests domestic industrials are soft, and rising oil input costs and yields weigh on capital-intensive names.

Reported: RTX raised its guidance three times over in its Q2 report (TIKR.com, [Jul 24]). United Rentals beat and raised guidance (Quiver Quantitative, [Jul 27]). American Airlines slashed its 2026 earnings outlook as fuel costs spiked (CNBC, [Jul 23]), part of a jet-fuel spike blowing a hole in airline profit forecasts (OilPrice.com, [Jul 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: GE Vernova — Guggenheim raised its target to $1,450 on the beat (Investing.com, [Jul 23]). Vertiv — raised guidance twice this year and the Street is still behind (TIKR.com, [Jul 21]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Inside the S&P 500 AI boom, industrials are getting as rich as tech stocks (CNBC, [Jul 26]): the AI-power names now carry tech-like multiples, and with them tech-like downside if the chip rout spreads to capex.

Narrative: A 52-year-old international restaurant chain closing all locations is a consumer distress signal, rising rates and energy costs squeeze wallets, and the H2 distressed outlook flags an elevated cost of capital.

Reported: Tesla's revenue beat but EPS missed (scanx.trade, [Jul 26]), and the stock plummeted 14% (Forbes, [Jul 23]). General Motors' Q2 beat on every line (TIKR.com, [Jul 22]). Shein flagged tariff hits after posting a quarterly loss ahead of its Hong Kong IPO (Reuters, [Jul 26]).
EPS Upside Watch: Ralph Lauren — Raymond James upgraded it on a stronger growth outlook ahead of earnings (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Shein's tariff hit is structural: its model was built on low-value import thresholds and cheap cross-border manufacturing arbitrage, so the read-through runs to the whole cross-border discount retail complex, not just one IPO candidate.
Narrative: Defensive rotation should help staples as tech sells off, but a 10Y at 4.59% competes directly with their dividend-yield proposition.

Reported: Philip Morris beat as organic sales rose 7.6% (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 22]). Albertsons surprised with Q2 sales, but the stock dropped 14.4% (StockStory, [Jul 23]). Lamb Weston beat expectations in a strong Q2 (StockStory, [Jul 24]).

EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola — reports July 28, with the bull case laid out ahead of the print (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 25]). Tyson Foods — earnings are expected to grow into its report (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Albertsons is fighting to keep lower-income shoppers from defecting to discounters (Grocery Dive, [Jul 24]) and General Mills faces changing American shoppers (Star Tribune, [Jul 26]): the staples shelter is cracking on volume, not just cost.
Narrative: A clinical-trials provider soaring past a buy point on solid Q2 results is the sector's direct signal, and healthcare benefits from the broad rotation out of tech.

Reported: Medpace soared 15% after beating estimates and raising guidance (TIKR.com, [Jul 23]). AstraZeneca's profit beat and bullish tone eased worries over its drug pipeline (Reuters, [Jul 27]). Thermo Fisher smashed estimates and raised its 2026 outlook as pharma spending lifted growth to 10% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 23]).
EPS Upside Watch: Quest Diagnostics — raised its revenue and EPS guidance for full-year 2026 (PR Newswire, [Jul 23]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The split is inside healthcare: research outsourcing and tools (Medpace, Thermo Fisher) are accelerating, while devices lag — J&J's MedTech performance slowed in Q2 (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]) and Edwards reversed after its beat (Investor's Business Daily, [Jul 24]).

Narrative: Copper at 6.36 (↑4.3% vs 4W), now an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, supports materials, and the supply-shock backdrop favours producers with pricing power. Construction materials still face China's 18 percent y/y property-investment slump.

Reported: Freeport-McMoRan beat estimates on rising prices for copper, the grid and data-centre metal (Barron's, [Jul 23]). BASF raised its full-year 2026 earnings outlook after a strong Q2 (European Coatings, [Jul 22]). Shin-Etsu Chemical plunged as its full-year outlook missed forecasts (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: Anglo American — cut its copper cost guidance sharply (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 23]), widening margins on a metal priced for AI data-centre and grid build-outs. Chemical producers — four are screened as poised to outshine Q2 estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 27]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.
Narrative: A 10Y at 4.59% (+22 bps vs 4W) is the single most hostile data point for rate-sensitive REITs, and Australia's RBA flagging housing easing more than anticipated is a global read-through.

Reported: D.R. Horton's full-year sales guidance missed expectations significantly (StockStory, [Jul 21]), and PulteGroup's profit fell as affordability pressure persists (Reuters, [Jul 22]). Digital Realty surged 11% after crushing estimates and raising full-year guidance (TIKR.com, [Jul 26]).
EPS Upside Watch: IGB REIT — HLIB raised its earnings forecasts after a strong Q2 (NST Online, [Jul 22]).
